full_judgment:
Md Hamidul Haque, J: By this Rule opposite parties were called upon to show cause as to why the order No 2 dated 27.1.99 passed in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2147 of 1999 arising out of Sonargaon Case No. 5(5) 99 now Pending in the Court of Magistrate. Class, Narayangonj should not be set aside. 

 2. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that accused Shajahan, opposite party No. 2 was enlarged on bail by the learned Session Judge, Narayangonj by his order dated 27.10.99 passed in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2147 of 1999. The learned Advocate further submits that there is specific allegation of throwing acid against opposite party No. 2 and offence was under section 326A of the Penal Code. According to him the learned Session Judge illegally granted bail to that accused. So according to him the bail granted to accused opposite party No. 2 should be cancelled. 

 3. This is an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It appears that the learned Session Judge in a Criminal Misc. to after hearing both parties granted hail to the accused opposite party No. 2. The reasoning given by the learned Sessions Judge may not be convincing but the order passed by him cannot be interfered with by this court under provisions of section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. There is specific provision to seek such relief in the High Court Division and that provision is contained in sub-section (5) of section 497 of the Code. The view of the superior court on the question as to whether bail granted by lower court can be cancelled under section 498 by the High Court Division is that if the Sessions Judge grants hail before arrest and if it appears to the High Court Division that there is no valid ground for enlarging the accused on bail before his arrest, under exercise of the right conferred under section 498, the High Court Division may cancel the bail granted by the Sessions Judge before arrest of the accused under section 498. Power of granting bail before arrest is concurrently given under this section to the High Court Division and the Court of Session and as such the High Court Division may interfere with the order of Sessions Judge regarding granting of bail before arrest. This principle is not applicable in the instant case because in the instant case the learned Session Judge passed the order in a Criminal Misc. case when the accused opposite party was in custody. When bail is granted by a Session Judge to an accused in custody after hearing the parties, such bail can be cancelled only on some definite allegations of abuse of the privileges of the bail or on the ground that the accused to whom bail is granted is making preparation to leave the jurisdiction of the court but such bail cannot be cancelled on the around that bail was wrongly granted. 

 4. In view of our discussion above, we are of the view that the present application is misconceived and as such the rule is liable to be discharged.
